txt: After you hand over the artwork, the voice from the light says: "Another deal complete. Welcome to the big leagues! If you haven't already, I'd advise you to consider hiring a Personal Brand Strategist."
From deep within the container, a voice: "Ahoy! Come on in!"
He smiles. "Never mind then. We'll just have to be on equal footing, geographically speaking."
He swills it around in his brain. "So it's an éxtrasomatic painting. An effort carried out by physical instinct -- not the mind."
In the general stillness, only your tongue moves, flickering as you utter...
Something's amiss. The light beams bend around his face and scatter in a thousand directions. It seems the laws of physics do not apply here. They are suspended, distorted, an echo.
The light around the individual in front of you changes somehow as you take the scroll. You can't figure out what's different -- you just know that it is.

The man chuckles. "It's quite alright. I'm used to the question by now. To be blunt, I inherited my fortune from my grandmother, who, herself, was an extremely high-net-worth individual back in Graad..."
The man chuckles. "To be perfectly blunt, I inherited my fortune from my grandmother, who, herself, was an extremely high-net-worth individual back in Graad..."

The man exhales with a whistle. "I gotta tell you, at first, being rich is a lot of work. You've got to work hard because everything's so darn expensive. You know, prices increase exponentially at this income level..."
The man pauses, considering your words. The light bends and swims around his face. You cannot tell what he's thinking...
The man stands at the far end of the shipping container. It's hard to say anything more about him. You cannot make out any of his details, but you do feel the overwhelming presence of... capital.
The shape stands in stunned silence.
There's no sign of a reaction for a good three seconds. Then...
"*Dangerous*? I like things that are dangerous. You could even say I'm one of these 'adrenaline-junkies'." The light emanating from him seems to intensify.
"*Dozens*, at least. Of course, in the future it'll all be automated. But my point is this..." he says, jabbing his finger into the air a bit...
"*Every day*?" The blinding light becomes almost melancholy. "But how does she find time to do any work?"
"*Mesque bangers*? No! Have I told you I've stopped reading the news? It's too negative, can't let it affect my mojo."
"A nightmare scenario. A world of slavery and violence. Which brings us back to the essential truth of modernism..."
"A painter, eh? I am always looking to expand into new asset classes. Who's the artist?"
"A youth centre, huh? What *kind* of youth centre?"
"A-ha. And the name of the piece?" He leans in to take a good look at the rectangular plastic board coated thick with emulsion.
"Absolutely not."
"Ah, Revachol. I remember walking its streets as a teenager. There used to be a bowling alley in Stella Maris... I wonder if it's still there?"
"Ah, a fellow entrepreneur. Tremendous! The art market? Intriguing. Sure, I'm keen. What are you thinking?"
"Ah, a fellow history buff! I, myself, am currently reading up on Franconigerian-era trains. Very interesting stuff. "
"Ah, interesting. I've made quite a few real-estate plays over the years."
"Ah, yes. Now you're displaying it... the *eccentricity* that becomes a wealthy individual." If the money-saint's visage weren't wrapped in physics-defying light, you would see his approval.

"All I did was take her fortune and invest it prudently. Believe it or not, it takes more than a bit of skill not to blow a vast fortune on sailing boats, bad choices, and *unsupervised* state policy."
"Among other things... but calm down, I'm but a lowly single-digit billionaire."
"An artist's value doubles if they come with a good backstory. I thought you were an experienced art dealer, you should know this."
"And if I don't buy it now, more people will see it -- ergo its value will drop."
"And that's, what? Unjust? I think it's perfectly just." His tone is ever-so-slightly less agreeable than before.
"And the name of the piece?" He leans in to take a good look at the rectangular plastic board coated thick with emulsion.

"Any details? I've heard some struggling families have to sell their organs to pay the rent. There is also the terrible misfortune of having to go get your own groceries when you're poor. Which one is it?"
"Anyhow, my name is Roustame Diodore -- investor, licence holder, and extremely high-net-worth individual. And you are?"
"Are you talking about my chin?"
"As you may know, us high-net-worth individuals do not have a lot of cash on hand. Investments and liquidity are enemies of one another -- I think I only have coins for coffee machines."
"Before I invest, I need to know more about the work. How do I know this asset is going to appreciate with time?"

"Being rich does not make one impervious to the human condition. Maybe I do have a strange chin and you are the first person to call me out on this. Not that you should. But you did. For this -- I am grateful."
"Brilliant! Without children who'll be there to buy stuff in the future?"

"But I appreciate the *grandiosity* of your ideas. Thus you might understand -- the entire org structure of the RCM needs to be redefined. You need a unified chain of command, an end to petty spats between precincts, new metrics for measuring performance that reward real *police work*. Does that sound right?"
"But I'm getting side-tracked. Tell me about your business proposal. I am all *ears*." His face seems to distort in the blinding light, pulling and twisting at his sides.
"But design is the very signature of humanity. Everything we do is design. Text columns, urban architecture, the precise shape of a stapler... what are we without any of that?"
"But perhaps I judge too quickly. Is there an intelligent reasoning behind the method?"
"But real-estate is an illiquid asset. What happens if you need a short-term capital infusion and all your holdings are tied up?"
"But then, once you've reached my position, it's nearly impossible for me *not* to make money. My assets are so diversified that I'm bound to come out ahead no matter what..."
"But what do you say to those who claim that the assets underlying those derivatives are overvalued? Does that pose a systemic risk to the wider capital markets?"
"By the way, let me now ask *you* a question: Where are we, exactly?"
"Capital." He nods. "Makes one speechless, does it not? Blinds like the sun that rises from beyond the horizon after a gloomy winter."
"Come now, there is not even a scent of corruption here. I am merely being polite... so let me check my pockets."
"Don't get me wrong: They're nice things, but once you achieve a certain level of wealth your time and mental space become *much* more important than material goods."
"Emerging? That's a word with plenty of appeal. What is it that defines this style exactly?"
"Every man gets what he earns. It's the height of tyranny to take that from him."
"Exactly!" He agrees. "A world of slavery and violence. Which brings us back to the essential truth of modernism..."
"Farewell, friend, and may your peace of mind guide you to happiness."
"Go on. I'm listening..."
"Go on."
"Go right ahead, don't be shy."
"Go right ahead."
"Have you heard about it? At the moment, it's trading at more than 1.5x the price of gold. That's because it's an essential component in the next generation of radiocomputers..."
"He may have been a communard, but we're in agreement about that. Still, I imagine the architecture is quite lovely."
"Hell no! Can you imagine how much work that would take? Why would I do that when I can just speculate on exotic financial derivatives from the comfort of this shipping container?"
"Here's a round of seed funding. This should be enough to prove out the concept and get things off the ground."
"Here's three reál, how much can you get for this?"
"Hm. I hadn't thought about it that way before. You might have just opened up a new door in my mind."
"Hm. I've never heard anybody say anything about my chin. Yet I know that people often tell each other half-truths, things they think the other party would wish to hear..."
"Hm. Seems unhygienic. Is that what's *in* these days?"
"Hmm, I do cling to it rather a lot. Perhaps that is one of my shortcomings -- I just haven't realised it before now."
"Hmm. I don't believe in giving anyone money for nothing, but maybe there's something to using *market incentives* to improve performance..."
"Hmmm," the man thinks for a moment.
"Hmmmm, a tried-and-true strategy for increasing the perception of value without improving the underlying asset. Not bad. But still..."
"Hold on. Have we met before?"
"However, there are a few *complications*.... I don't have the cash on me right now to pay for art of this calibre. What I can instead offer are shares in Mauer-Koshlai Mercury Group."
"I appreciate you saving us from wasting time. Is there anything else I should know about the painting?"

"I bought these shares many years ago for a steal. As predicted, Mauer-Koshlai Mercury's operating profit has increased year on year, and there's no signs of it slowing down. People *always* need mercury."
"I don't believe in handouts, especially for people who *volunteered* for their positions..."
"I don't normally do this without a formal pitch deck, but to hell with it, what's the point of being rich if you have to follow all the rules?"
"I like that you're thinking about the future, but couldn't the centre have a more... economic focus?"
"I see -- very good. What kinds of issues are we talking about? I've really got into the housing crisis recently."
"I see, so by artificially constraining supply you're also stimulating demand. I have to say, it's a brilliant strategy..."
"I see. What is so special about it then?"
"I see..." The light appears to concentrate...
"I think I follow you. You're saying I should invest in exotic financial derivatives? Or maybe some kind of real-estate play?"

"I think the lieutenant's right. Your problems run much deeper than equipment or funding. The entire org structure of the RCM needs to be redefined. You need a unified chain of command, new metrics for measuring performance that reward real *police work*. Does that sound right?"
"I'll be honest, all I see are splatters that lack any true intention."
"I'm already on the board of two major arms manufacturers. I've got no shortage of guns, if I wanted such things..."
"I'm listening."
"I'm ready."
"I'm very impressed. You have a deep understanding of the world that few men ever attain."
"I've found it's much better for my health just to throw money at those kinds of problems and hope they go away. That way I don't have to feel guilty about avoiding them."
"In any case, is there anything *else* you can tell me about this piece?"
"Intriguing. Go on."
"It is not possible. But what a dream..." He shakes his head. "Either way, even if I could do it, I certainly wouldn't give an incompetent and corrupt police force *WORLD-ENDING* weaponry."
"It is, truly. It's almost entirely care free." He nods. "It really leaves you time to better yourself spiritually."
"It lets you *immerse yourself* in a modern school of thought? Are you sure?"
"It was a real pleasure. Sadly, though, my current lifestyle prevents me from remaining more than a brief time in any one place. Perhaps we'll meet again, somewhere far away..."
"It's a Gottwaldian-Iilmaraan company that specialises in extracting mercury. It's seen massive growth lately due to the discovery of rödfärg mercury."

"It's a shame I can't get out and explore myself. One of the downsides of being an extremely high-net-worth individual is that mobs of low-net-worth individuals are constantly banding together to ask for money."
"It's perfectly alright. Based on your appearance I can tell I'm dealing with a civilized man..."
"It's perfectly alright. Based on your appearance I can tell I'm dealing with a smart man..."
"It's some statistical thing. In essence, it says that when an extremely *low*-net-worth individual meets an extremely *high*-net-worth individual, some of the laws of physics cease to apply."
"Just a hollow husk..." The blinding light becomes almost melancholy.
"Just a mixing palette? But where does the value lie then?"
"Keith, I like it. One of my nephews is named Keith. We haven't spoken in years, since I declined to pay for his most recent trip to rehab. But perhaps this will help patch things up between us..."
"Keith," he repeats.
"Keith? Just *Keith*?"

"Listen, I used to be an idealist, just like you. But the truth is that we have no objective system by which to measure someone's value other than the market. We should just embrace that, rather than resist it..."
"Listen, if capital and nationalism went hand in hand, there'd be no need to ask the question..."
"Luxury yachts, high-fidelity portable radio systems, pale-proof outerwear, and so on. It just gets a bit *middle class* after a while. A bit *bourgeois.*"
"Maybe I should? Sadly, I've never been there. I'm sure it's nice but in the end -- does it matter?"
"Maybe you can make that money grow? Come up with an investment plan? How's that sound?"
"No, no, no. You've got to think *bigger* than that."
"No, not even him. He might have some Moelles and de Vignys, the *authenticity* of which historians are debating, but I don't think that counts. Perfect."
"No, not really. There are actually quite many digits."
"No, on second thought, it couldn't have been you."
"Nobody knows for sure, but the place can't be pretty."
"Not a problem. The offer stands for as long as I'm around these parts."
"Not even a pseudonym?" The light appears to vibrate with surprise.
"Now, was there anything else I could help you with?"
"Now." He claps his hands together. "What can I do for you, good sir?" What you can see of his body appears composed. In a sharp summer suit. And yacht shoes.
"Oh yes, I see it now. Very *graphic*, isn't it? Really delivers insight into what it's like being that... unruly."
"Oh, *that's* what you mean. Yes, I've heard of this effect, though I've never witnessed it myself, of course. It has something to do with our Weiss-Wiesemann coefficient."
"Oh, alright then. Another question."
"Oh, don't you worry, lieutenant. I can tell a good man when I see one."
"Oh." He sounds disappointed. "Well, I'm sure her work represents some very interesting *internal* struggle. Probably with mental illness. Yes, that sounds right."
"One would imagine living such a high-net-worth existence is overwhelmingly exciting, but yes, as you now see... it can sometimes just stun you with its boredom."
"Original. I don't think any of my friends have any pieces from anonymous artists. Or maybe only Luca, the son-in-law of the Comte de L'Ys."
"Perfect! I've been looking for a way to communicate without the information being intercepted or stolen by rivals."
"Perhaps I *have* been neglecting the triumphs of anatomical perspicacity lately..." He sinks into thought.
"Perhaps I could be the one to 'discover' it? To share it with the wider world..."
"Please, if there's something I'm missing, I'd love to know what it is."
"Pleasure to meet you Harr... I mean, Tequila Sunset," he says warmly. "It is an odd name, to be sure. There's something... rather grim about it."
"Pleasure to meet you, Harrier Du Bois," he says warmly. "I must admit, the name suits you very well."
"Pleasure to meet you, Harry," he says warmly. "Public service is a noble cause."
"Pleasure to meet you, Harry," he says warmly. "Though I'm sorry to hear a good man like yourself is in servitude to the drink. But then, nobody's perfect."
"Pleasure to meet you, Harry," he says warmly. "Though I'm sorry to hear a good public servant like yourself is in servitude to *the drink*. A man can't serve two masters, in my experience."
"Pleasure to meet you, Raphaël," he says warmly. "I am surprised -- in a positive manner, do understand -- about your exceedingly high-net-worth name."
"Pleasure to meet you," he says warmly. "Public service is a noble cause."
"Pleasure to meet you," he says warmly. "Though I'm sorry to hear a good man like yourself is in servitude to the drink. But then, nobody's perfect."
"Pleasure to meet you," he says warmly. "Though I'm sorry to hear that a good public servant like yourself is in thrall to the drink. A man can't serve two masters, in my experience."
"Poor thing! In that case, buying this will help me fulfil my *noblesse oblige* for the month."
"Pray tell." The human shape within the light appears to lean even closer. Tiny dots flood your retina as the shipping container gets too bright.

"Precisely! You know, I hear people talk sometimes about *economic equality* and *fairness* and all that kind of stuff. But tell me, where would we be without liberalism? In caves! Whacking each other with bones!"
"Precisely, which is why I'm not going to do it. Why would I do that when I can just speculate on exotic financial derivatives from the comfort of this shipping container?"

"Rehm's using it in their next model. I can't wait for mine to turn up! My predictions say its improved speed and azimuthal range should increase my trade efficiency by a whopping 46%. You really should order one if you don't want to be left behind."
"Remember: it's not a *handout*, it's an investment. And I expect to see returns."
"Sadly, when we got there, it was too late. The concept had run out of steam, only dust remained."
"Smart, no? It also provides a means to hide from all the targeted advertising we extremely high-net-worth individuals are constantly subjected to..."
"So! What's next on the agenda?"
"Some of my lower-net-worth friends say to me, 'But doesn't that take all the fun out of it?' and I tell them, 'Not really.'"
"Sounds like a hell of a trip. I really must experience it for myself." The light emanating from him seems to intensify.
"Spending money is a matter of desire, I'm sure you agree. I don't have the desire for spending it like that."
"Splendid." You hear the sound of expensive fabrics brushing against each other. When it stops, a roll of paper emerges from the radiance.
"States are akin to boulders in a river, slowing the free flow of ideas. Given enough time, the water will wear those boulders down."
"Still, only two people have seen it thus far. That makes it pretty *exclusive* and therefore potentially valuable."
"Still, the idea of a privatized police force is *extremely* forward thinking. You could even say it's *ultra* ultraliberal..."
"Such a simple truth, yet so easily forgotten. What is money, anyway, but an idea in our heads we all *trust* one another to believe in?"
"Sure! Let me check my pockets."
"Sure, and they benefit when I buy things to stimulate the economy. Do you know how many jobs it takes to build and maintain a racing yacht?"
"Tell me, if you could invest in the RCM, where would you direct your resources?"
"Thanks for stopping by. If you ever have an idea you want to pitch me, I'm all ears."
"That changes everything."
"That concludes *our part* of the transaction. Once you've turned over the asset, my people will get the legal ball rolling."
"That prophet-for-hire did say I should identify weakness and remove it from my life..."
"That's a shame. Is there anything else to this painting, or is that it?"
"That's good."
"That's the idea, my friend! You've got to work for the rest."
"That's what I wanted to ask you about. Tell me, what's their *story*? Did they *suffer*?"
"That's why I *should* invest? Are you trying to say that the RCM's bad reputation makes it an undervalued asset?"
"The RCM's problems aren't the kind you can solve with *radiocomputers*. The rot goes much deeper than that..."
"The art market, you say? Possibly. As I said, I don't carry much money on my person, but do go on -- what are you thinking?"
"The art market, you say? Sure. 'Hit me with it', as they say. I'm keen to hear what you have in mind."
"The art market? Intriguing. Well, as I said, I don't carry much money on my person. But do go on, what are you thinking?"
"The art market? Intriguing. You've already convinced me to invest in you, so please, go on -- tell me what you're thinking."
"The hand that allocates resources among men is invisible and cruel, but it is *steady*, *measured*, indeed it is *just*."
"The pleasure was mine. Unfortunately, I must be away soon. The next time we meet, I'll be expecting an update on my investment!"
"The thing about investing is that the less work you have to do, the better. Don't over-think. That's what return on investment means."
"The volunteer police force? And why would I do that?"
"There it is. I knew it as soon as you did the Milton 32-8 knock. A fellow entrepreneur!"

"There simply aren't enough hours a day to hand out all the handouts. It's like feeding seagulls. There are always more, and they never seem to do anything interesting with it -- except more seagulls."
"They are the very *unit* of capital. You can buy them, sell them, even sit on them if you think it wise. Trust me when I say this -- becoming a shareholder means you're part of the *big leagues*."
"They could set you up for a *long time*. Mauer-Koshlai Mercury is just getting started. Mark my words."
"They lacked the *will* to get things done. As their financial situation became more desperate, their ideas devolved from realistic to absolute insanity."
"They pitched me and a handful of other investors on an idea for a role-playing game that would, in their words, change the world."
"This is a stock certificate. Well, a photocopy of one. Nevertheless, it's solid proof that you own shares in Mauer-Koshlai Mercury Group."
"Travelling! This is a great way to get around -- it's fun, it's safe, and it gives me lots of time to think..."
"Trust... yes..."

"Unfortunately not. I only know the ones who work with multi-millionaires and beyond. But take a look around and I'm sure you'll find one. Personal Brand Strategists are attracted to money like *sharks* to blood. You'll find having net worth opens many new doors for you."
"Very impressive. You've got a natural eye for unusual investment opportunities."
"Was it Kras Mazov that said 'religion is pyrholidon for the masses'?"
"We lost all of our money. High-art types never deliver. They're only good for peddling welkins or whatever creeps they come up with."
"Welcome back, friend. What can I do for you?" Although you cannot see his face, you can tell he's smiling warmly.
"Welcome! Come in, make yourself at home. Sorry I'm not better able to receive you -- I wasn't expecting visitors today."
"Welcome, welcome! Not too much, actually, just pleasantly surprised to have company today."
"Well, I think that settles it. You've found a buyer, my friend. A pleasure transacting with you." The light around him warms you like a friendly embrace.
"Well, as we say in my circle -- one person's crushing business failure is someone else's development opportunity."
"Well, at first everything was rosy, the ideas were solid, but they were lacking in... how do I put it..."
"Well, you've already convinced me to invest in you, so please, go on -- tell me about this opportunity. I'm keen."

"What *don't* they do?" The shiny magnate chuckles. "They practically do everything -- from spotting good investments and analysing design trends, to booking a lunchtime table at the prestigious L'Ambroisie."
"What I want to tell you is this: it's a very bad idea. Dead in the water. You seem like a reasonable man, but that is not a reasonable plan."
"What a sad, sad story. I should ask Rhéa to look into this, maybe the foundation can set up some scholarships for cases like these."
"What an original idea! By drawing our focus away from the final piece we gain a new appreciation for the craft behind it. An art in its own right that is usually hidden from us."
"What do you mean?" His... essence seems to signify actual surprise.
"What? No, I didn't say that at all. Being rich is great. Just don't tell anyone I told you that." The bending light appears to *wink*.
"When life closes a door, it opens a window, yes? What's the expected return on this?"
"Where we are right now, the freedom of mankind can only be derived from the free flow of capital."
"Which means you could net yourself a considerable profit if you need some immediate liquidity. But if you don't mind waiting I expect the value of these shares to double within the next five years."
"Which one? Revachol, where I nominally reside? Or Graad, where my father emigrated from? Or Ile-de-Casherbrume where I've registered my shell companies?"
"Who *am* I? Oh, I haven't been asked that question for such a long time." There's genuine surprise in his voice. "I don't meet a lot of people outside my circle these days..."
"Why go so soon? I feel we've so much more to talk about. Ah, well. Until next time!"
"Wonderful things aren't they -- names? They can completely change your reading of a person. Or, in this case, a painting."
"Yeah, on second thought, it couldn't have been you."
"Yes, I'm sure. You know..." His eyes narrow, the light seems to bend more *aggressively*.
"Yes, every school child hears that. The question is how do *we* get more of that money?"
"Yes, the special knock that helps us ultras identify each other. I almost forgot it myself."
"Yes, yes, but the question is how do we take advantage of those fluctuations?"
"Yes. I imagine that *does* look strange to you. My container."
"Yes?"
"You know, that's *exactly* what I've heard. From what I understand, the RCM as currently constituted is essentially a lost cause..."
"You mean even *you* haven't looked at it?"

"You need to think *bigger*. The entire org structure of the RCM needs to be redefined. You need a unified chain of command, an end to petty spats between precincts, new metrics for measuring performance that reward real *police work*. Does that sound right?"
"You said that already."
"You want to take an incompetent and corrupt police force and give them *deadlier* weapons? No, no, that won't work..."
"You're welcome. Now, was there something else I could help you with?"
"You're welcome. You know..." His eyes narrow, the light seems to bend more *aggressively*.
"You?" The light appears to blink, as if someone switched off the light source for a second. "But why should we care about *you*?!"
"Your idea reminds me of a group of young men who came to me a long time ago, calling themselves 'Fortress Accident' -- the name should've been a red flag."
